## What changed

**Nothing that mattered here.** cap-evolve's `RESULT` line for the accepted candidate names this
task in its `fixed={}` set:

> ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.962 Δ=+0.086 · fixed={bench-aap2-001-single-job-outcome,
> **bench-aap2-002-failed-jobs-on-controller**, bench-aap2-009-nonexistent-job} ·
> broke={bench-aap2-006-log-root-cause, bench-aap2-008-preceding-task}

At equal `n` that is not what happened. The seed, re-measured at `n=9` inside the same iteration,
scored **1.000 on all 8 of its valid trials**. `cand_0001` also scored **1.000 on 9 of 9**. The
delta at equal `n` is **exactly 0.000**. There was nothing here to fix.

The `+0.100` the run reports is measured against a *reused* `n=3` `seed` value of `0.900`, whose
vector is `[1.000, 1.000, 0.700]`. One trial. The entire "fix" on this task is one weak trial in a
three-trial sample that the candidate was never compared against at the same trial count.

None of the champion's six edits touch this task's behaviour: they concern `get_job` vs
`get_job_log` action selection, a transient-error retry, and report length. This task's golden path
is a single `find_jobs` call with a `controller` filter.

## What worked

**The contract, which is the point of this task.** This is the only v2 scenario weighted
`tool_calls 0.6 / answer 0.4` — tool calls outweigh the answer — and the provenance explains why:

> The original contract could be satisfied by an agent that skips filtering entirely… The
> `controller` argument in tool_calls was the only real evidence of filtering, but it was
> underweighted at 0.4.

The reweighting plus a `derived: true` `count` fact makes an unfiltered `find_jobs` lose roughly
`0.73` instead of keeping `0.6`. In 20 measured trials of the seed and champion across this run, 19
scored a clean `1.000` — correct filter, correct count, all three job ids. The discipline the
contract was built to test is discipline the skill already has.

## What didn't

**The single `0.700` trial is unexplained and worth a look.** It decomposes uniquely: with 1 expected
call and 4 required facts at `0.6/0.4`, `0.700 = 0.6 × (1 of 1 calls) + 0.4 × (1 of 4 facts)`. The
agent made the right filtered call and then named **only one of `count`, `90201`, `90202`, `90203`**.
That is a much larger answer failure than the notation defects this task's provenance spent three
separate edits fixing, and it is not obviously any of them. It is one trial out of 20 and it never
recurred. If anything here deserves a rollout pulled and read, it is that trial.

**This task's history is also a warning about reading its own numbers.** Three defect fixes were
needed before the contract measured what it meant to, all on 2026-08-05, and two of them were found
only because a live agent produced a *correct* answer that scored as wrong:

- `count` was a required fact the instruction never asked for — the agent listed all three ids and
  never stated a count, scoring `0.900` for it. Fixed by rewriting the instruction to ask.
- The re-run then scored `0.900` again, for a different reason: the agent said "There are **3** AAP2
  jobs…" and `count`'s `any_of` was `["Three", "three"]` — word forms only.
- Fixing *that* could not simply add `"3"`, because job `90203` is one of the three correct ids and a
  bare `"3"` matches inside it. `"3 failed"` was also dropped for the same reason: an answer listing
  "…90203 failed…" would satisfy the count fact by coincidence, "which is exactly the false-positive
  this fact exists to prevent."

Every one of those is a scoring defect, not an agent defect, and each was caught by measurement
rather than by review.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**We can learn that this task is at ceiling and has been for the whole of v2.1 onward**, and that a
task at ceiling contributes nothing to an optimizer except the risk of being reported as "fixed."
Which is what happened. It should be moved out of the val split, or the split should stop being one
task wide (see `results/v2/summary.md` on `test: []`).

**We can learn something durable about contract authoring from the digit-form saga.** The rule the
provenance extracted — "a bare digit cannot be used as a substring assertion, but a digit with its
noun can; and every candidate form must be checked against the seed's own literals for coincidental
matches" — was arrived at here, applied to `bench-aap2-007`, and written into the project's
`CLAUDE.md`. That is the benchmark improving itself, and it is the most transferable output of the
whole v2 exercise.

**We cannot read the `+0.100` as an effect of the champion.** It is a comparison between an `n=3`
reused baseline and an `n=9` candidate on a task where both score `1.000` when measured the same
way. Two of the five task-level verdicts in this run's `fixed`/`broke` lists are artifacts of that
mismatch; this is one of them.
